title: Turkish Mint Borek
description: A traditional Turkish pastry filled with a soothing mixture of mint, herbs, and spices, designed to alleviate hangover symptoms, made with diabetic-friendly ingredients and finished with a silky glaze.
instructions: In a large mixing bowl, combine the flour and warm water to form the dough.
Knead the dough for 5-7 minutes until smooth and elastic.
Place the dough in a greased bowl, cover with a damp cloth, and let it rest for 30 minutes.
On a lightly floured surface, roll out the dough to a thickness of 1/8 inch (3 mm).
Cut the dough into 12 equal squares.
In a small pan, heat the tadka oil over medium heat and sauté the minced garlic until fragrant.
In a separate bowl, mix together the chopped mint, parsley, dill, garlic, ginger paste, lemon juice, and salt.
Place a tablespoon of the herb mixture on one half of each dough square, leaving a 1/2 inch (1 cm) border.
Brush the edges of the dough with olive oil and fold the other half over the filling to form a triangle.
Press the edges to seal and use a fork to crimp the pastry.
Brush the tops with olive oil and bake for 20-25 minutes, or until golden brown.
While the borek is baking, prepare the silky glaze by whisking together 1 cup of powdered sugar and 2 tablespoons of lemon juice.
Once the borek is done, let it cool for 5 minutes before brushing with the silky glaze.
